extracted.intended_audience: Heads of Executive Departments and Establishments; agency procurement and implementation officials
extracted.subtask_description: Federal agencies must implement revised OMB Circular A-76 by appointing responsible officials, creating internal procedures and inventories, scheduling reviews, and coordinating with OFPP via an interagency committee and training activities. The page lists specific procedural requirements, timelines, and allowable security exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of a senior official
rubrics_metrics.description: Designate an official at the Assistant Secretary or equivalent level to have overall responsibility for implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a specific requirement imposed on each agency by Circular A-76 to ensure clear accountability for implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a central point of contact office
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish an office as a central point of contact to respond to all requests concerning inventories and reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The office should handle inquiries about agency inventories and review processes related to Circular A-76.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue internal instructions within 90 days
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue internal instructions for implementation of the Circular, within 90 days, providing a copy to the Office of Federal Procurement Policy (OFPP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must produce and forward their internal implementation instructions to OFPP within the 90‑day deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventory of agency commercial and industrial activities and 3-year review schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a complete inventory of all Government commercial and industrial activities in the agency and a schedule for review of each activity within the next three years, publishing the schedule and providing a copy to OFPP within 120 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The inventory and review schedule must be published and submitted to OFPP within the 120‑day timeframe; purpose is to determine whether activities should be government-run or rely on the private sector.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventory of contracts subject to A-76 and review timetable
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare an inventory of contracts subject to Circular A-76 and a schedule showing when the contracts will expire and be reviewed, publishing the schedule and providing a copy to OFPP within 120 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must identify contracts covered by A-76 and timetable their review in order to apply the Circular's cost-comparison and acquisition policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative review procedure for determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish a procedure for administrative review of determinations under Circular A-76 when objections are raised by an affected party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must provide an administrative remedy/process so parties affected by A-76 determinations can raise and have objections reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit implementation actions and reports to OFPP
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency is required to take actions to implement the revised circular and to submit reports to the Office of Federal Procurement Policy (OFPP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a general reporting obligation accompanying the specific requirements (inventories, schedules, internal instructions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interagency Committee objective: assist consistent, effective, equitable, expedient implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Interagency Committee on Implementation of Circular A-76 will have as its principal objective assistance to agencies in their efforts to achieve consistent, effective, equitable, and expedient implementation of the revised policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Committee provides a forum for exchange of information, coordination of approaches, and problem-solving among agencies implementing the Circular.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of agency representative to the Interagency Committee and meeting preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Please designate a representative of your agency, preferably at the working level in the office responsible for implementation; the representative should determine, prior to the meeting, the number and location of the personnel from your agency that require such training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should appoint a representative to attend Interagency Committee meetings (e.g., the October 17, 1979 meeting) and prepare by identifying staff training needs for new cost comparison procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination of training for agency personnel in cost comparison procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A major effort at the Committee meeting will be plans for coordinating training for agency personnel in the new cost comparison procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must assess and communicate the number and location of personnel needing training so training coordination can be planned across agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for exceptions based on security, cover, or protection of sources and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies (in particular CIA) may seek exceptions from strict compliance on the basis of security, cover, or the protection of sources and methods and may implement the Circular only to the extent consistent with operational, security, and cover considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CIA noted that while it endorses the objectives and will be guided by the spirit of A-76, it may be unable to comply with the letter of the requirements where statutory responsibilities or protection of sources/methods require deviation; such exceptions have been sought through agency OMB examiners and discussed with OFPP.
